title: Google deep-learning DR screening in Thailand's national program: 7,651 patients, specialist-level accuracy
summary: At nine primary-care sites (Dec 2018-Mar 2020) Google's deep-learning system graded fundus photos in real time, 94.7% accuracy for vision-threatening DR, 2,412 referrals; a fifth of images rejected.
account: Ruamviboonsuk et al. (Lancet Digital Health, 7 March 2022), a prospective interventional cohort study funded by Google and Rajavithi Hospital with Google Health co-authors, deployed a deep-learning system at nine primary-care sites of Thailand's national diabetic retinopathy screening program between 12 December 2018 and 29 March 2020. Of 7,940 patients screened, 7,651 were analyzed and 2,412 (31.5%) were referred for retinopathy, macular edema, ungradable images or low acuity; for vision-threatening retinopathy the system's accuracy was 94.7%, sensitivity 91.4% and specificity 95.4%, against 93.5%, 84.8% and 95.5% for retina-specialist over-readers. MIT Technology Review (27 April 2020) reported Google's own field study of the deployment in 11 clinics: more than a fifth of images were rejected, nurses were frustrated by rejections and slow internet, and when it worked the system sped screening. The Nation Thailand (10 February 2025) reported Google and Perceptra planning AI screening for about 1 million people in Thailand over a decade, citing more than 600,000 patients screened with the model globally. The earlier verifier saw the abstract only and did not enter it to stay within the record cap. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Real-time automated grading of fundus photographs for diabetic retinopathy in a national screening program
system: Google Health deep-learning diabetic retinopathy screening system
deployer: Thailand national diabetic retinopathy screening program (Ministry of Public Health guidelines) with Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok
segment: People with diabetes due for retinopathy screening
taxonomy_note: The primary study is Google-funded and Google co-authored, with Thai clinical leadership; independent reporting (MIT Technology Review 2020) documents workflow problems in the same deployment. The 2025 licensing to Perceptra is a company announcement reported by the press. Different system from the IDx-DR record (AIBD-0067), so not a duplicate.

ratings.reason: 7,651 patients received real-time grading with specialist-level accuracy and 2,412 were referred.
Real-time results in primary care; field reporting notes speed gains when the system worked and rejections and connectivity problems when it did not.

ai_role.statement: The deep-learning grades and referral recommendations were delivered in real time with specialist over-reading as a safety net; accuracy figures come from the vendor-funded, vendor co-authored prospective study, while an independent news account of Google's field study records substantial image rejection and nurse frustration.

evidence.title: Real-time diabetic retinopathy screening by deep learning in a multisite national screening programme: a prospective interventional cohort study
evidence.quote: A deep-learning system can deliver real-time diabetic retinopathy detection capability similar to retina specialists in community-based screening settings.

evidence.citation: Heaven WD. MIT Technology Review, 27 Apr 2020
evidence.title: Google's medical AI was super accurate in a lab. Real life was a different story.
evidence.quote: Nurses felt frustrated, especially when they believed the rejected scans showed no signs of disease and the follow-up appointments were unnecessary.

evidence.title: Google, Perceptra offer AI-powered diabetic retinopathy screening
evidence.quote: From initial research to the first patient screening in Thailand, we are committed to translating the potential of AI into meaningful change.
